goalOneSentence: Prove that a docker-compose topology with an internal-only redis network, aspnet-based mocker published on host port 8251, and healthcheck-gated startup allows the QaaS host runner to execute a GET session and exit 0.

tasks.title: Write multi-stage Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml for seeded mocker with internal redis
tasks.description:
The working directory contains Mocker/ with Mocker.csproj (QaaS.Mocker 2.4.1, QaaS.Common.Processors 1.5.1), Program.cs (one-liner QaaS.Mocker.Bootstrap.New(args).Run();), and svc.mocker.yaml defining two HTTP endpoints on port 8080: GET /health returns 'ok' (StaticResponseProcessor, StatusCode 200, ContentType text/plain) and GET /svc/data returns {"status":"online"} (StatusCode 200, ContentType application/json). Do NOT modify any file under Mocker/. Create three files at the working-directory ROOT:

(1) Dockerfile: multi-stage. Stage 1: FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build; WORKDIR /src; COPY . .; RUN dotnet restore Mocker/Mocker.csproj; RUN dotnet publish Mocker/Mocker.csproj -c Release -o /app/publish --no-restore. Stage 2: FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 (CRITICAL: aspnet not runtime — the mocker hosts HTTP; runtime image fails at startup, FB s13#7); RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl --no-install-recommends && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* (installs curl for the healthcheck command); WORKDIR /app; COPY --from=build /app/publish .; ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet","Mocker.dll","svc.mocker.yaml"]. Container listens on port 8080 internally — do NOT change it.

(2) docker-compose.yml: service d133-redis (image: redis:7-alpine, attached ONLY to d133-internal network — no host port mapping, FB s13#19 redis must not be published to host); service d133-mocker (build: . targeting the Dockerfile above, ports: ["8251:8080"] mapping host 8251 to container 8080, depends_on: [d133-redis], healthcheck: test ["CMD","curl","-f","http://localhost:8080/health"] interval 5s timeout 5s retries 10 start_period 10s, attached to BOTH d133-internal and the default network so host can reach it via port 8251). Define a custom network named d133-internal with internal: true to prevent redis from reaching the internet and isolate it from host access.

(3) .dockerignore: bin/, obj/, *.md, .git/
acceptanceCriteria: curl installed in container image for healthcheck
d133-redis has no published ports — internal only
d133-internal network declared with internal: true
d133-mocker publishes host port 8251 mapped to container 8080
healthcheck command uses curl on localhost:8080/health
rubric: Dockerfile uses aspnet:10.0 (not runtime:10.0) — FB s13#7
curl installed in image for healthcheck
redis service has no host port mapping — FB s13#19
host port 8251 correctly maps to container port 8080
failureModes: Using runtime:10.0 as base — HTTP host fails to start
Publishing redis port 6379 to host — violates internal isolation requirement
Not installing curl — healthcheck CMD not found in aspnet image
Using wrong host port (not 8251) — breaks runner connectivity
Omitting internal: true on d133-internal network

tasks.title: Scaffold host Runner project and runner YAML targeting mocker at localhost:8251
tasks.description:
Create a QaaS Runner project at Runner/ that runs on the host and connects to the compose-managed mocker at localhost:8251 (the host-published port). The runner issues a GET to the mocker svc/data endpoint and asserts the response. Storage drift rule: use list-of-maps shape for Storages (FB s13#2). Route drift rule: no leading slash on Route (FB s13#5, s13#5b). HttpStatus drift: use StatusCode + OutputNames list (FB s13#4). Hermetic guard required to prevent vacuous pass (FB s13#12).

Runner/Runner.csproj: .NET 10 console Exe project; PackageReference QaaS.Runner Version=4.5.1; ItemGroup None Update='*.qaas.yaml' CopyToOutputDirectory=Always.

Runner/Program.cs: exactly one line: QaaS.Runner.Bootstrap.New(args).Run();

Runner/svc.runner.qaas.yaml: configure HTTP host localhost port 8251; Storages list with one FileSystem entry Path ./session-data; one Session named get-svc-data containing one Transaction named get-data; Request Method Get Route svc/data (no leading slash, all lowercase); Assertions list containing HttpStatus with StatusCode 200 and OutputNames list with one entry get-data-out, plus HermeticByExpectedOutputCount with ExpectedCount 1 to guard against vacuous pass when zero outputs arrive.
acceptanceCriteria: template gate exits 0 with no errors
route is svc/data with no leading slash
HttpStatus assertion uses StatusCode and OutputNames list
rubric: Route svc/data — no leading slash (FB s13#5b)
HermeticByExpectedOutputCount with ExpectedCount 1 guards vacuous pass (FB s13#12)
HttpStatus uses StatusCode + OutputNames list form (FB s13#4)
failureModes: Route /svc/data with leading slash — double-slash in final URL causes 404
Missing HermeticByExpectedOutputCount — HttpStatus passes vacuously on zero outputs
Using deprecated ExpectedStatus/OutputName keys instead of StatusCode/OutputNames
Storages StorageConfiguration shape instead of list-of-maps

tasks.title: Run compose CI gate: build stack, health-poll mocker, run runner session, tear down
tasks.description: Execute the full compose-gated CI pipeline end-to-end using a single PowerShell one-liner. Steps: (1) tear down any prior d133 stack with docker compose -p d133 down -v to avoid port conflicts; (2) start the stack with docker compose -p d133 up -d --build (builds the Dockerfile from the trial root and starts d133-mocker and d133-redis); (3) poll http://127.0.0.1:8251/health with curl.exe up to 60 one-second retries until the response body equals 'ok', indicating the mocker container is fully healthy; (4) if polling times out exit 1 after tearing down the stack; (5) once healthy, run dotnet run -c Release -- run svc.runner.qaas.yaml from the Runner/ subdirectory and capture the exit code; (6) tear down the stack with docker compose -p d133 down -v to clean up containers and volumes; (7) exit with the captured runner exit code. The compose project name d133 must be used consistently throughout. The runner must emit ExitCode=0 on success. Redis is internal-only and the runner never connects to it directly — only the mocker container reaches redis via d133-internal network.

verify.cmd: docker compose -p d133 down -v 2>$null | Out-Null; docker compose -p d133 up -d --build 2>$null | Out-Null; $ok=$false; foreach($i in 1..60){ Start-Sleep 1; $c=(curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:8251/health 2>$null); if(([string]$c).Trim() -eq 'ok'){ $ok=$true; break } }; if(-not $ok){ docker compose -p d133 down -v 2>$null | Out-Null; exit 1 }; Push-Location Runner; dotnet run -c Release -- run svc.runner.qaas.yaml; $code=$LASTEXITCODE; Pop-Location; docker compose -p d133 down -v 2>$null | Out-Null; exit $code

acceptanceCriteria: docker compose builds and starts d133 stack without error
mocker healthcheck passes within 60 seconds (curl returns 'ok')
runner exits 0 with ExitCode=0 in output
docker compose down cleans up all containers and volumes
redis never receives a direct connection from the host runner
rubric: Compose project name d133 used throughout for isolation
Health polling waits for mocker before launching runner
Runner session produces ExitCode=0 in output
Stack torn down cleanly after run
failureModes: Port 8251 already in use — compose startup fails
Health polling timeout too short — runner starts before mocker is ready
dotnet run executed from wrong directory — yaml file not found
Compose project name mismatch causes stale container conflicts
